absent: Attribute decoding into processor and address and common register accessor semantics beyond delegation presence.
Common attribute handling, creation, destruction, initialization ordering and pending-table save effects.
Reference counting and lookup rules for per-processor versus global interrupt descriptors.
Queueing, list-register fill and fold, pending-latch versus active transitions and list pruning mechanics.
Virtual machine control get and set translation and system-register probe details.
ITS virtual SGI property update effects and hardware interrupt mapping.
Full version 2 CPU register table beyond the truncated portion and version 3 region table contents.
Numeric encodings of offsets, masks, shifts and group selectors beyond the architecture version value.

findings.text: Line level window helpers expose a 32-wide view anchored at a caller identifier, one producing a mask of asserted level lines and one installing levels from a mask.
Version 3 distributor device control exposes set, query and existence operations plus a device operations table under a version 3 name.
Version 5 distributor device control exposes a parallel set, query, existence and operations table under a version 5 name, with a dedicated userspace PPI query helper.

Version 2 emulation exposes miscellaneous distributor, group, software interrupt generation, routing, pending-source, CPU interface and active-priority handlers together with kick and deactivate services.
Register existence probing for version 3 families and userspace-gated version 2 miscellaneous and group writes are available as separate entry helpers.

Line window covers only usable private plus shared identifiers; software-generated identifiers and identifiers beyond the configured total never contribute, reads report only level-configured asserted lines, writes store the supplied level regardless of edge or level configuration to decouple restore order.
Register-family attribute groups share one accessor for both directions, while maintenance interrupt identity uses direct user copy with distinct set-time validation and get-time reporting.
Maintenance identity installation is permitted only before distributor initialization and only for a private peripheral identifier; retrieval returns the stored value under protection.

Existence probing accepts distributor and redistributor address kinds, defers register families to a register probe, unconditionally accepts interrupt-count and maintenance groups, accepts level-info only for the line-level selector, and accepts only initialization and pending-table save controls.

Version 3 register existence requires successful attribute decoding, selects distributor versus redistributor region tables or delegates system registers, rejects misaligned offsets and unknown regions, and otherwise reports success.

Version 5 exposes almost nothing: address, system-register and count groups are unavailable, control set accepts only initialization through common handling, and only initialization and userspace PPI queries are reported present.
Userspace PPI query returns two words: stored low bitmap contents followed by zeros for the unbacked upper half, under configuration protection.

Miscellaneous distributor state reports enablement as a single enable bit, derives count information from total interrupt population and online processor count, and composes identification from product, revision and implementer fields.
Only the control word is mutable through normal miscellaneous writes; count and identification offsets ignore stores, and a disabled-to-enabled transition requests a wakeup scan.

Userspace identification writes must preserve all bits outside the revision field and select one of two supported revision codes; only then do they latch group writability and update stored revision, otherwise they fail.
Userspace group stores are effective only after the writability latch has been set; before that they succeed without effect.
Group installation is per-bit across the access width; hardware-backed software-generated interrupts take a property-update path while others take a queue path.

Software interrupt generation decodes target set, low identifier and mode; modes select explicit mask, all-but-self, self-only, and a reserved mode that does nothing, with each selected recipient recording source and pending state.
Routing bytes for private interrupts are immutable, shared routing bytes are masked to the online processor set, and the selected recipient follows the lowest set bit with a zero fallback.
Software interrupt source state is a per-recipient bitmap: reads expose it, clear removes supplied bits and drops pending only when empty, set adds bits and raises pending when non-empty.

CPU interface emulation is a virtual machine control view: control bits map to group enables and mode flags, priority mask is shifted between hypervisor and architectural representations, binary points pass through, and identification composes product, architecture version and implementer.
Deactivate-by-write dispatches on global host interrupt controller type to the matching version-specific deactivate routine.

Version 2 deactivation applies only in end-of-interrupt mode one, strips the embedded processor tag, ignores unknown identifiers, requires SGI source match, folds a cleared-active list entry, performs a hardware deactivation for hardware entries, and requests list pruning on the owning processor.

Active-priority view depends on host type: version 2 hosts expose only index zero from a single register, version 3 hosts expose indices up to a per-processor maximum from indexed group-one registers.
Per-interrupt state uses an interrupt-saving spin lock around level, group, routing, source and pending updates, with a queue-and-release variant on paths that may make the interrupt pending.
Configuration mutex guards maintenance identity and userspace PPI bitmap accesses across attribute set and query paths.
Deactivation serializes against list-register handling with local interrupt masking plus a scoped per-interrupt lock held only while inspecting ownership and computing the folded entry.
Distributor enablement is a latched flag whose rising edge triggers a scan that marks and kicks only processors with pending virtual interrupts.
Version 2 group writability starts denied and latches permanently on the first acceptable userspace revision write, preserving migration behavior for older userspace.

Software interrupt pending follows source membership: non-empty source implies pending, empty source after clear implies idle, and deactivation of an entry still resident in list registers falls back to a memory-mapped clear path.
Device-level entry occurs through create and destroy plus set, query and existence callbacks installed in per-version operation tables.
Guest and userspace register entry occurs through region tables binding distributor and CPU offsets to read, write and userspace access handlers with declared access widths.

Several inputs are silently ignored rather than reported: unusable line-window members, reserved generation mode, private routing writes, unknown CPU interface offsets, out-of-range deactivation identifiers, deactivation outside the required mode, and out-of-range priority indices.

Attribute and userspace register misuse is reported: user copy faults, busy after initialization, non-private maintenance values, misaligned offsets, unknown regions or groups, unsupported revisions, and unavailable version 5 groups.
Priority index is range-checked and speculation-hardened before indexing the per-processor priority array.
CPU interface architecture version for version 2 guests has numeric value two.

Device ABI horizons observed here include distributor, redistributor, system-register, level-info, address, count, maintenance and control groups with distributor, redistributor-region, initialization and pending-table selectors.
Level-info existence uses a masked and shifted selector compared against a line-level kind, and version 2 identification revision accepts two defined implementation codes.
Device operations comprise a name plus create, destroy, set, query and existence handlers, instantiated once per supported virtual controller version.
Version 2 register tables associate base offsets with guest read and write handlers, optional userspace handlers, bit density or length, and permitted access widths.

Observed virtual interrupt state includes configuration, line level, group, priority, targets, owning and target processors, source bitmap, pending and active flags, list-register presence, hardware backing and lock; distributor state includes enablement, shared count, revision, group latch and maintenance identity; processor view includes active-priority registers and mode control.
